choices.text: The student is right - every artery carries oxygenated blood
The pulmonary artery is the exception: it carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs.
The pulmonary artery carries no blood to the lungs
Arteries to the lungs are drawn blue, so they are veins

questions.feedback: If you agreed with the student, that is the trap: Arteries always carry oxygenated blood. Reteach point: The pulmonary artery is the exception: it carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs. Name vessels by direction, not colour.
questions.prompt: A student says the pulmonary artery must carry oxygen-rich blood because it is an artery. What is the best correction?

questions.answer: It carries blood away from the heart, and arteries are vessels that carry blood away from the heart.
questions.feedback: A strong answer uses direction: away from the heart makes it an artery, whatever oxygen its blood carries.
questions.prompt: In one sentence, explain why the pulmonary artery is an artery even though its blood is oxygen-poor.

questions.feedback: Xylem lifts water and minerals upward; phloem is the food-sharing tissue.
questions.prompt: Which plant tissue carries water and minerals up from the roots?

questions.answer: Pulmonary loop: heart to lungs and back. Systemic loop: heart to body and back.
questions.feedback: The double circulation is two loops sharing one double pump: lungs loop and body loop.
questions.prompt: Name the two loops of the double circulation and where each one runs.
